top_paper.title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills
top_paper.summary: Socratic Skill Learning improves reusable agent skills by interleaving expert guidance with student practice and targeted review, outperforming trajectory and contrastive distillation methods.

papers.title: DeLoop: Repeated Actions as Self-Supervision for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.summary: DeLoop is a self-supervised preference optimization method that reduces repetitive tool-use loops in language-model agents by learning from their own rollouts, improving efficiency and success under context compression.

papers.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
papers.summary: WildAWM synthesizes controllable computer-use environments and tasks to train general agents via interaction, improving out-of-distribution performance across web, CLI, and GUI benchmarks.

papers.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
papers.summary: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise. However, realizing this design requires more than diverse backgrounds. When experiments are costly, a team can test only a limited number of ideas, thereby creating the need to balance exploration and exploitation when selecting a subset of researchers to propos

papers.title: Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR Technical Report
papers.summary: We present Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR, a family of audio-language models that builds upon its predecesor Qwen-Audio-3.0-ASR with improved speech recognition and expanded capabilities in speaker-diarized transcription and general audio understanding. The family retains support for 30 languages and 16 Chinese dialects, together with instruction-controlled capabilities including historical-context conditioning, hierarchical hotword customization, and native transcription polishing. papers.title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
papers.summary: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet studying RSI requires an environment that is continuously changing, objectively verifiable, and naturally grounded, posing a fundamental challenge for agent evolution. Here we introduce DeepEvolve, a sustainable evolution agent system grounded in future event prediction, in which agents continuously interact with a dynamically evolving enviro

papers.title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
papers.summary: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation assigns localized channel importance at each spatial position via conditional Shapley values, yielding full spectral-spatial attribution matrices that outperform existing methods on multispectral image tasks.

papers.title: Agentic World Action Models
papers.summary: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. papers.title: CulturalRiddles: A Multicultural Benchmark of Riddles
papers.summary: As LLMs expand their language coverage, evaluating how well they understand and represent diverse cultures becomes increasingly important. However, many benchmarks remain English-centric, with limited cultural coverage and a focus on factual knowledge over its application in real-world cultural contexts. We propose CulturalRiddles, a benchmark of original, culturally grounded riddles created entirely by humans through a participatory community effort, spanning 62 cultures (45 countries, 51 languages). These riddles are deeply rooted in their respective cultures and require abductive and compos

papers.title: Real In, Real Out: What If We Only Use Real Data for Scene Text Editing?
papers.summary: TextRIRO enables scene text editing using self-paired real data via image disruptions and a conditional diffusion model, improving realism and supporting downstream recognition.

papers.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
papers.summary: StreamEval benchmarks interactive streaming video generation across five tasks, revealing that reliable request execution and sustained state consistency remain major challenges despite high visual quality.

papers.title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills
papers.summary: Socratic Skill Learning improves reusable agent skills by interleaving expert guidance with student practice and targeted review, outperforming trajectory and contrastive distillation methods.

papers.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
papers.summary: AgenticRoboRL improves robot planners via supervised fine-tuning and multi-turn reinforcement learning across diverse harnesses, significantly boosting success rates without external memory.

papers.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
papers.summary: Memory-Centric Continual Learning reframes agent memory as an active driver of behavioral improvement through a taxonomy of storage substrates, assets, and policies, a two-loop lifecycle, and scaling frameworks evaluated by retention, adaptation, and transfer.

papers.title: ACE-Brain-0.6: Scaling Spatial Grounding for Physical Foundation Models
papers.summary: Scaling diverse verifiable visual grounding data improves spatial perception and embodied manipulation performance in open multimodal models.

papers.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.summary: ALLOT is a training-free method that allocates block-sparse attention densities across layer-step pairs in video diffusion transformers to maximize output fidelity under a latency budget.

papers.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.summary: Future Chunk Prediction improves autoregressive video diffusion by enforcing future-chunk supervision, yielding more physically plausible video generation with reduced training cost.

papers.title: RubatoCodec: Budgeted Adaptive Speech Tokenization with Streaming Decoding
papers.summary: RubatoCodec uses adaptive event-based coding with fixed utterance budgets to improve low-rate speech reconstruction and streaming text-to-speech generation.

papers.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
papers.summary: AKV introduces cache engineering to manage LLM agent key-value caches without altering trajectories, improving efficiency and accuracy via drop and repos operations with a co-designed serving engine.

papers.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
papers.summary: ALPS is a pretrained visual encoder that unifies physical-state prediction, language alignment, and pixel reconstruction to serve as a shared foundation for world models.

papers.title: Toward Part-Aware Choral Transcription with singing voice assignment
papers.summary: PawCT is an end-to-end neural framework that jointly transcribes choral audio into separate SATB note tracks using part-specific predictions, range priors, and ordered-continuity constraints.

papers.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
papers.summary: VX-One is a small multi-task neural network that outputs calibrated typed decision primitives for perimeter triage, evaluated in a two-phase cascade against signature engines and baseline classifiers across multiple intrusion detection benchmarks.

papers.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
papers.summary: GRSE improves cooperative language agents by comparing repeated executions to correctly assign behavioral credit to agent-skill pairs, outperforming prior methods on multi-hop reasoning and recovering from harmful skills.

papers.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Harness Scaling improves agentic reinforcement learning by training across diverse execution configurations, boosting generalization to unseen harnesses.

papers.title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: Ask-to-Distill optimizes synthetic questions to maximize teacher-student distributional supervision for on-policy distillation without requiring correct answers, improving reasoning, coding, and agentic task performance.

papers.title: ATEST: Adaptive Resource-Aware Test-Time Scaling for LLM Inference
papers.summary: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model (LLM) reasoning by sampling multiple answers, but fixed sampling budgets ignore both query difficulty and the changing energy cost of inference under GPU contention. We measure up to a 4.1-fold increase in energy for the same four-sample query as GPU load rises. We present ATEST, a resource-aware TTS framework that jointly considers the expected value of additional samples and their current GPU cost. papers.title: What Makes a Good Symbol for Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Planning?
papers.summary: Symbols for robot planning are invented by identifying discrete commitments that simplify solving continuous optimization problems, reducing cost while preserving quality.

papers.title: Not All Features Are Created Equal: A Mechanistic Study of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: A mechanistic interpretability study of vision-language-action policies reveals that motor programs are bound to absolute coordinates and ignores visual scene changes, with sparse autoencoder analysis separating instruction encoding and motor generation across architectures.

papers.title: BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks
papers.summary: BiDex-100 is a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation that evaluates vision-language-action models across diverse tasks, robustness variants, and demonstration scales.

papers.title: Training the Whole Agent, Not Just the Model
papers.summary: HarnessAdapt-RL jointly trains a coding policy and adapts its evaluation harness via mechanism-level skills and evolving tools, improving benchmark pass rates over fixed-harness reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Axiomatic World Modeling for Physics Reasoning
papers.summary: RLAWM improves physics reasoning by penalizing divergence between a model's internal world model and true physical axioms through hierarchical modeling and solving rewards.
